title: བསྟན་འགྱུར། སྡེ་དགེ། ཚད་མ། མེ (Derge Tengyur, vol. 185)
shelf_note: Authentic canonical Tibetan Buddhist Pramāṇa (epistemology/logic) commentary from the Derge Tengyur collection, volume 185 (letter 'me').

ocr_errors.problem: Subjoined sa-ta ligature སྟེ (ste) misread as རྟེ (rte) with ra-mgo
Epistemological commentary term ཐལ་བ་ (prasaṅga / logical consequence) misread as ཐ་མ་ (final)

tr_errors_A.english: If one asks what the final consequence is,

tr_errors_A.english: that experience by another does not belong to another person because there is no experience
tr_errors_A.problem: Slightly awkward syntactic parsing of the argument regarding experiencing another person's cognition

tr_errors_B.english: because memory occurs as a mere mental event
tr_errors_B.problem: Imprecise translation of དྲན་པ་ཙམ་ (mere memory) as 'mere mental event'

tr_errors_B.english: If one wonders what the final conclusion is,
tr_errors_B.problem: Minor translation distortion derived from OCR misreading ཐལ་བ་ (prasaṅga) as ཐ་མ་ (final)

pages.prefer_reason: Translation A provides precise Sanskrit technical vocabulary with standard diacritics (arthāpatti, pramāṇa, parokṣa) and preserves the formal structural commentary cues more accurately.

book_verdict: Well-preserved Derge Tengyur Pramāṇa woodblock folio with high-accuracy transcription and faithful English translations of complex Buddhist epistemological arguments on self-awareness and memory.
